_comment: Fonts baked into the VT100 terminal. Edit this file, then run bake-fonts.bat (or bake-fonts.sh), then rebuild.
_type_note: 'type' is 'bdf' for native bitmap fonts (glyphs copied one-to-one, no scaling) or 'ttf' for outline fonts (supersampled and filtered down to the cell). Bitmap sources are the only way to keep historical glyphs pixel-perfect; scaling an outline face to 8 pixels wide loses its shape.
_path_note: Relative paths are resolved against the repository root. TTF entries use ${FONT_DIR} and ${FONT_SUFFIX} so the same file works on Windows and Linux: FONT_DIR defaults to the platform's font directory and FONT_SUFFIX to .ttf. Override either with the FONT_DIR / FONT_SUFFIX environment variables.

families.name: DEC VT220
families._note: Authentic DEC terminal glyphs: native 10x20 bitmap from 1986 VT220 ROM firmware. Ink is exactly 8 pixels wide, so it maps onto our 8-pixel cell with no scaling and yields a classic 80x24 screen.

families.name: Modern
families._note: Consolas. Present on Windows by default; on Linux install ttf-mscorefonts-installer or drop a substitute mono face in tools/fonts/ and point path at it.

families.name: Terminal
families._note: Cascadia Mono. Ships with Windows Terminal and recent VS Code releases; on Linux install the Cascadia Code package or point path at another mono face.
